newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down after following silver.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down after following silver.

text.p: Hong Kong's spot gold market ended lower on Wednesday from New York's previous close after European gold sales followed a drop in silver.
Bullion ended at US$350.20/70 an ounce against New York's US$351.70/352.20 close on Tuesday.
Morning trade was extremely quiet, with hardly any impact from the stronger yen felt in gold markets.
"This is because positions at the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) are pretty small," said one senior bullion trader.
He said that after the drop in dollar/yen, Tokyo punters may start reconsidering currency movements in their gold trades.
Gold prices dropped on early Swiss selling which started at about $351.50 per ounce, dealers said.
Gold prices dipped in tandem with silver, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$2 lower at HK$3,242 a tael.
Ample physical supplies in Hong Kong provided no incentive to buy, dealers said.
Physical gold premiums in Hong Kong had softened to about 60 cents over the loco London market, compared with about 120 cents in late March.
"This is because physical supplies are plentiful here," said one bullion trader.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -4.00 from its previous fix at -6.90
